Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

INLAvaan (development version)

  • INLAvaan now requires R 4.1.0 or later, and cli 3.6.0 or later. It no longer suggests spacefillr and ucminf, which only the Sobol nodes of the old VB correction and optim_method = "ucminf" used.

  • The posterior predictive p-value, the DIC and fitMeasures() are faster. The PPP and the DIC now score each posterior draw in one pass, from one computation of its implied moments, and with complete data the log-likelihood of a draw is computed in closed form. The fit keeps the log-likelihood of each draw, so bfit_indices() and fitMeasures() use the draws of the fit (and of the independence baseline) and no longer draw and score new ones, and the draws of the independence baseline are scored all at once. On single-level test models, a fit followed by fitMeasures() takes 16% to 74% less time (from 0.35 to 0.09 seconds on a one-factor model), and fitMeasures() alone 71% to 92% less. The PPP is unchanged and the DIC is unchanged up to rounding. The Bayesian fit indices change by Monte Carlo noise once. The independence baseline is fitted at the first call of fitMeasures() or bfit_indices() and kept with the fit (a few kilobytes), so later calls (and compare(), which uses the baseline of its first model) take no time for it, and their indices are the same and no longer depend on the random seed. A smaller nsamp than the fit’s takes the first draws of the fit, and a larger one draws anew.

  • Fits are faster, with the same results. The map from the internal parameters to lavaan’s parameters, the chain rule of the gradient and the prior now find their index tables once per model, and not on every evaluation of the log-posterior. On single-level models with complete data a fit takes 19% to 57% less time (57% on a panel model with 156 parameters), and 9% to 14% less on models with missing data and on two-level models with random intercepts. Random-slope fits do not change.

  • Fits that hand the engine a Hessian at the mode (a model on the saturated-means fast path, or hessian_method other than "central") check the gradient at the mode with about 2m evaluations of the log-posterior, where they took about 6m to 8m. The engine now takes the steps of that check from the diagonal of the Hessian. The posterior is unchanged.

  • Fits of single-level models with missing data (missing = "ml") are faster. The log-likelihood and its gradient now take one inverse of the model covariance matrix for all missing-data patterns, and work the patterns with the same number of missing variables together, from tables that are built once per model. On seven test models a fit takes 42% to 78% less time (from 18.9 to 4.1 seconds on a model with 40 variables and 169 parameters). The log-posterior equals the earlier one up to rounding. On a model whose mode search takes many iterations, the optimiser can then stop at a slightly different point, and a posterior summary can move by about 0.00004 posterior SDs. Patterns that miss many variables, as in planned missingness, keep the earlier code.

  • Two-level fits are faster. Every two-level computation of INLAvaan is now its own code, not lavaan’s: the log-likelihood and gradient of random slopes (rv()) on observed and on latent or split covariates, with or without between-only outcomes, and of random intercepts with or without between-only variables, each with complete data and with missing values (missing = "ml"); the per-cluster terms of loo() and waic(); the empirical Bayes values of predict(); and the saturated model of the two-level posterior predictive p-value. The new code works all clusters at once and does the matrix algebra of the gradient once, not once per cluster, and the derivative of the random-slope pieces is exact. On four random-slope test models a fit takes 91% to 93% less time (from 35.5 to 2.5 seconds on a two-level factor model with a random slope and missing data), and 77% less with a slope on a latent covariate, where the cluster effects are integrated by quadrature; fitMeasures(), loo() and waic() are faster too. Two-level models with random intercepts take 30% to 32% less time with complete data and 21% to 32% less with missing data. The log-posterior equals the earlier one up to rounding, so a posterior summary of a fit whose mode search takes many iterations can move by about 0.0002 posterior SDs.

  • loo() and waic() are faster, with the same results up to rounding. The Hessian of each unit’s log-likelihood (a row, or a cluster of a two-level model with complete data) is now computed in closed form in the data, and only the second derivatives of the model-implied moments are taken by finite differences, once for all units. Before, the scores of all units were differenced in every direction. One LOO pass takes 2.6 to 3.8 times less time on large single-level models (17.2 to 5.8 seconds on a model with 40 variables, 169 parameters and missing data) and 4 to 6 times less on two-level models with complete data. The estimates agree with the earlier ones to 1e-7 or better. options(inlavaan.loo_hessian = "differences") keeps the earlier route.

  • waic() after loo() (or loo() after waic()) with default arguments no longer computes the Taylor pass again: the fit keeps its last default pass. With the faster Hessians, loo() and waic() together take 80% to 91% less time on models where they dominate.

  • The posterior predictive p-value (PPP) of two-level models with missing data (missing = "ml") is faster. Before, the saturated model of each replicate data set was fitted by EM from a crude start. It is now found by quasi-Newton steps from the moments of the posterior draw, which reach the same maximum, and the EM is kept for replicates whose maximum lies on the boundary. On three test models the PPP takes 2.1 to 8.7 seconds in place of 25 to 45, and the fit 71% to 87% less time; over 20 seeds each the PPP is the same number as before. ppp_method = "em" keeps the EM, as blavaan does.

  • Two-level models with conditional.x = TRUE now fit. Before, the fit stopped with “subscript out of bounds”. INLAvaan fits them as the joint model with fixed.x = TRUE, which has the same free parameters and the same posterior: the log-likelihood of the outcomes given the covariates is the joint log-likelihood less that of the covariates, which holds no free parameter. loo(), waic(), the PPP and predict() work on these fits. As in lavaan, missing data and random slopes cannot be combined with two-level conditional.x = TRUE.

  • Multigroup two-level models (a group: block for each group, each with its level: blocks) now fit, with complete data and with missing values. Before, INLAvaan refused them. The log-likelihood and gradient are INLAvaan’s own two-level code, summed over the groups, and loo(), waic(), the PPP, predict(), sampling() and simulate() work on these fits. The coefficient names follow lavaan’s (fb=~y2.g2.l2). In loo(fit, units = ) the clusters (or rows) of group 1 come first, then those of group 2, and so on. Random slopes cannot be combined with groups, as in lavaan.

  • Random-slope models (rv()) with fixed.x = FALSE now fit, and the covariates are modelled. INLAvaan adds the two-level normal density of the observed covariates, with their means, variances and covariances as parameters, to the random-slope likelihood. The other parameters keep the posterior they have under fixed.x = TRUE, and loo(), waic() and the Bayesian fit indices score the covariates too. lavaan accepts these models but leaves the covariate density out, so its covariate estimates stay at their start values and it reports no standard errors. The slope must be on an observed within-cluster covariate, each covariate without a slope must be observed at one level only, and the covariates must be complete; other fixed.x = FALSE random-slope fits are still refused, with the reason.

  • predict(newdata = ) now works for two-level models, with or without random slopes, groups or missing values. Before, INLAvaan refused it. The new rows must hold the cluster variable (and the group variable of a multigroup fit). lavaan’s own set-up code finds their clusters and missing-data patterns, and their clusters are scored with the fitted parameters. Given the fitted data again, predict() returns the same draws as without newdata.

  • New argument silent in inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth(). silent = TRUE prints nothing and muffles the warnings and messages raised during the fit, for simulations and other repeated fits. Errors are still raised. Whether or not silent is TRUE, the fit records the texts of its warnings in the field warnings of get_inlavaan_internal(). fitMeasures(), bfit_indices() and compare() now fit the independence baseline with silent = TRUE, so the warnings of that fit are no longer shown. update(fit, silent = TRUE) drops verbose from the call of fit, and update(fit, verbose = TRUE) drops silent, so either works on a fit made with the other.

  • The installed file inlavanilla.lock names the release of the inlavanilla engine whose files INLAvaan copies, with a hash of each copy. INLAvaan now copies the 13 engine files of inlavanilla v26.11.27, byte for byte, as R/vanilla-*.R, and the lock lists them. Two of them, R/vanilla-skew-normal.R and R/vanilla-qsnorm-fast.R, hold the skew-normal functions, which INLAvaan defined itself before. The others hold the stages of a fit (see the next item).

  • inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth() now fit with the engine files. The engine finds the posterior mode, takes the Laplace approximation, applies the VB correction of the mean and fits the skew-normal marginals, on the internal scale of the parameters. INLAvaan still builds the model, the priors and the log-posterior, and does everything after the marginals: the draws, the summaries on the lavaan scale, the PPP, the DIC, the LOO and the WAIC. The posterior mode does not change. What changes:

    • The VB correction takes one deterministic step from the nodes of a rule with 2m + 1 points, in place of 64 scrambled Sobol nodes. The shift of the mean moves by up to 0.04 posterior SDs on the Holzinger and Swineford three-factor model, 0.09 on the Political Democracy model and 0.16 on a two-level factor model. So the posterior means, the marginal log-likelihood (by up to 0.08 on these models), the DIC and the LOO move a little. The shift has no quadrature error, so diagnostics() gives NA for vb_mcse_max, vb_mcse_mean and vb_mcse_sigma.
    • The one-step VB correction checks its step, with a second pass of the rule at the step. The step must shrink the residual of the VB equation (vb_lhat below 1), and the slope of the fixed-point map along the step must lie between -1 and 1 at the mode and at the step (vb_j0 and vb_j1). A fit that passes keeps its one step, as the Holzinger and Swineford three-factor model and the Political Democracy model do. A fit that fails solves the VB equation instead, from the mode, and the warning at the end of the fit says that the posterior is far from Gaussian along the mean correction, and names the parameter that the step moved furthest. The solve takes at most twice the evaluations of the mode and Hessian stage, in passes of the rule (vb_budget in inlavaan_control()). When the solve stops more than 0.1 posterior SDs short of the VB mean, the warning says so too. Small samples fail the check more often: a one-factor model of x1, x2 and x3 fails it on the first 50 rows of HolzingerSwineford1939, and passes on all 301. diagnostics() gives vb_lhat, vb_j0 and vb_j1, and vb_solve, which is 1 when the check failed.
    • The volume correction of the skew-normal marginals is computed for all parameters at once. It is closer to the exact value, and moves the posterior summaries by up to 0.002 posterior SDs on these models.
    • With a saturated mean structure (the fast path of the intercepts), the Hessian at the mode no longer takes the block between the intercepts and the other parameters as zero. Without priors (add_priors = FALSE) it no longer adds the prior precision of the intercepts. The intercepts have no scan, so their rows of approx_data give NA for logC, nmad and gamma1, and diagnostics() averages nmad over the scanned parameters only.
    • Some arguments and values of the old stages have no counterpart in the engine. They are deprecated (see the table of arguments below).
    • The search for the posterior mode by nlminb() now allows 5000 iterations and 5000 evaluations of the log-posterior, not 1000 and 2000. When the gradient at the mode is too large, the engine runs nlminb() again from there, and the iterations of both runs are counted.
    • sn_fit_ngrid must be a single number of at least 7. Otherwise the fit stops with an error.
    • A fit stops with an error when the log-posterior cannot be evaluated at the starting values.
    • cores = NULL follows future::plan(), which is serial unless a plan is set. Before, a model with more than 120 free parameters ran its scans in parallel.
    • cores must be NULL or a single positive whole number, as the engine checks. Other values, such as 0, 2.5, NA or -3, now give an error. Before, they ran on one core, or on the whole part of the number.
    • The engine warns when the Hessian at the mode is not symmetric, or does not agree with the gradient.
    • get_inlavaan_internal() has a new field engine, with the engine’s diagnostics, scans, counts and timing, whether the engine had a gradient (has_grad), and the release and commit of inlavanilla. In the field opt, dx is now the analytic gradient at the mode, as dx_analytic is. In the field vb, method is the VB route that the fit used: "onestep" by default, or "full" with vb_correction = "full". It is no longer "sobol" or "gauss_hermite". The line “VB correction” of summary() now gives this route, ONESTEP or FULL, or NONE with no VB correction, or YES for a fit made before the engine. Before, it gave TRUE or FALSE.
    • An invalid vb_correction, such as NA, now gives an error. Before, it turned the VB correction off.

  • loo(), waic() and the LOO and WAIC of test now take the terms of each unit, and the estimates, from the engine’s Taylor layer, which inlavanilla’s own loo() and waic() use too. INLAvaan still computes the log-likelihood, the score and the Hessian of each unit. The numbers do not change, apart from rounding: on the models checked, each value moves by at most 1e-12 relative to max(1, |value|).

  • New inlavaan_control() makes the control list of inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth(). Its entries are mode_maxit, mode_maxeval and mode_tol for the search for the posterior mode, vb_maxit, vb_tol and vb_budget for the VB correction, n_grid and log_threshold for the skew-normal scans, nlminb for other controls of nlminb(), and hessian, debug and add_priors. A plain list with some of these names works too, such as control = list(n_grid = 31).

    • An unknown entry, or a bad value, gives an error that names the entry.
    • vb_budget caps the solve that follows a failed check of the one-step VB correction, as a multiple of the evaluations of the search for the mode and of the Hessian. The default of 2 doubles the cap of earlier development versions, which vb_budget = 1 restores. vb_budget = Inf lifts the cap, and vb_budget = 0 leaves a flagged fit at its mode. A fit that passes the check does not depend on it.
    • n_grid, log_threshold, hessian, debug and add_priors replace the arguments sn_fit_ngrid, sn_fit_logthresh, hessian_method, debug and add_priors of inlavaan(), which are deprecated and give the same fit. Give each setting once: an entry and its old argument together give an error, and so do mode_maxit and nlminb$iter.max (and alike for mode_maxeval and mode_tol).
    • Up to 0.3.5, control was a list of controls of nlminb(). These names still work, with a deprecation warning once per session, and give the same fit: control$iter.max, control$eval.max and control$rel.tol set mode_maxit, mode_maxeval and mode_tol, and the others, such as control$trace, go to nlminb. An old name and the entry that it sets, such as control$iter.max and control$mode_maxit, together give an error that names both.
    • When the search for the mode stops at its limit, the warning at the end of the fit now says to raise mode_maxit or mode_maxeval in inlavaan_control().

  • The arguments of inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth() are now those of INLAvaan 0.4.0. Old calls still run. A deprecated argument or value warns once per session, with a warning of class inlavaan_deprecated that says what to use instead, and stops from INLAvaan 0.5.0. With options(inlavaan.deprecation = "error") it stops now. The deprecated arguments keep their places, with the default NULL, so calls that give arguments by position still work. Their help has a “deprecated” badge. INLAvaan 0.3.5 has the old methods.

    Argument In 0.4.0
    vb_correction "onestep" (default), "full" or "none". TRUE and FALSE still work, for "onestep" and "none".
    marginal_method "skewnorm" (default) or "gaussian". "marggaus" is deprecated: use "gaussian", which gives the same fit. "asymgaus" is deprecated, and runs "skewnorm". "sampling" gives an error of class inlavaan_unavailable: the name is kept for a sampler that is under development.
    marginal_scan New. How the scan of each skew-normal marginal is taken: "linear" (default), "exact", "laplace" or "plain".
    marginal_correction Deprecated. "none" and FALSE are marginal_scan = "plain", which gives the same fit. "shortcut", "shortcut_fd" and "hessian" run marginal_scan = "linear".
    sn_fit_ngrid Deprecated. Use control = inlavaan_control(n_grid = ), which gives the same fit.
    sn_fit_logthresh Deprecated. Use inlavaan_control(log_threshold = ), which gives the same fit.
    hessian_method Deprecated. Use inlavaan_control(hessian = ), which gives the same fit.
    debug Deprecated. Use inlavaan_control(debug = TRUE), which gives the same fit.
    add_priors Deprecated. Use inlavaan_control(add_priors = FALSE), which gives the same fit.
    n_qmc Deprecated, with no effect. The VB correction has no quasi-Monte Carlo nodes.
    vb_method Deprecated, with no effect. The VB correction has one rule, and vb_correction = "full" iterates it.
    samp_copula Deprecated, with no effect, also in sampling(), simulate() and bfit_indices(). The draws always couple the fitted marginals by a Gaussian copula. For the draws of the Laplace approximation, use marginal_method = "gaussian".
    samp_norta Deprecated, with no effect. The draws no longer adjust the correlations of the copula (NORTA).
    sn_fit_temp Deprecated, with no effect. The skew-normal marginals are fitted with temperature 1.
    optim_method Deprecated, with no effect. The posterior mode is always found by nlminb().
    numerical_grad Deprecated, with no effect. The fit always uses the analytic gradient.
    silent New (see above).
    • Where an old call maps to the same setting, the numbers do not change. In get_inlavaan_internal(), marginal_method is now "gaussian" for Gaussian marginals, not "marggaus". samp_copula, samp_norta, optim_method and R_star are always TRUE, FALSE, "nlminb" and NULL.
    • predict() no longer reads samp_copula from the fit. It draws as the fit does.
    • acfa(), asem() and agrowth() set model.type themselves. Given model.type, they now stop with an error of class inlavaan_wrapper_model_type. Before, they ignored it.
    • When the VB correction did not settle, the warning at the end of a fit now names vb_correction = "none", not vb_correction = FALSE.

  • data now defaults to NULL in inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth(), so a model can be fitted from sample.cov and sample.nobs alone. Before, such a call stopped with an error, because data was missing. With neither data nor sample.cov, the fit stops with an error of class inlavaan_no_data, which says to give one of them.

  • inlavaan() now checks model.type, which must be "sem", "cfa", "growth" or "lavaan". Another value gives an error of class inlavaan_model_type that lists these. Before, the value went to lavaan, so a misspelt name gave “object not found”, and "efa" an error about the arguments of efa().

  • A name in dp that is not a type of parameter of priors_for(), such as priors_for(lamda = "normal(0,1)"), now gives a warning of class inlavaan_dp_unused. Before, such a prior was dropped without a word. dp = blavaan::dpriors() gives no warning: its ibpsi, which only blavaan uses, is left out of the check.

  • update() now starts the search for the mode at the mode of the fit (the warm start) only when the refitted model has the same free parameters, by name and in the same order, and the same data. Otherwise it starts from the usual values. So update(fit, meanstructure = TRUE) now works, where before it stopped with an error about the length of start. update(fit, std.lv = TRUE), which keeps the number of parameters but changes them, no longer starts from values of other parameters. The fit was the same, but the search for the mode took longer. With new data (data, the sample statistics, or a data call such as lavaan::simulateData()), the refit now starts cold and gives the fit of a fresh call. Before, it differed from that fit by up to 3e-5 in the mode and 4e-3 in the marginal log-likelihood. The help no longer says that the warm start leaves the fit unchanged: the mode it finds agrees with that of a fresh fit to the optimiser’s tolerance.

  • update(fit, start = NULL) now starts from the usual values. Before, the warm start was used anyway.

  • When an object that a fit’s call names is no longer found, as after rm() or in a new session, update() now stops with an error of class inlavaan_update_data_not_found. The objects checked are the data, the model, and the sample statistics (sample.cov, sample.mean, sample.nobs). The error names each object not found and says to give it again, as in update(fit, model = mm, data = dd), or to fit the model again with inlavaan(). Objects named after a function, such as df or data in a new session, count as not found. The check does not run a data call such as read.csv() or lavaan::simulateData(): it checks only the object at its root, and an error inside the call is the error of the refit. Before, update() stopped with “object not found”, or gave the function to lavaan, which stopped with an error about the data.

  • update() now replaces an argument of the call that it is given under another spelling, such as std_ov = FALSE for std.ov = TRUE. Before, the call held both, and lavaan stopped with “At least one snake_cased name (std_ov) is duplicated!”.

  • update() now stops with an error of class inlavaan_update_abbreviated when it is given an abbreviated argument name, such as dat for data, and names the arguments it may mean. Before, lavaan stopped with “unknown argument”, or R with “argument matches multiple formal arguments”.

  • update(fit, arg = NULL) now drops arg from the call of the fit, or gives it as NULL when the call does not have it, as stats::update() does. Before, an argument that the call did not have failed with “subscript out of bounds”.

  • Fits made with INLAvaan 0.3.5 or earlier must be fitted again with this version. diagnostics(), sampling(), loo(), waic(), predict(), simulate(), fitMeasures(), bfit_indices() and standardisedsolution() now stop on such a fit with an error of class inlavaan_old_fit, which says how to fit it again. waic() still returns a WAIC that the fit stores. summary() and show() still work, but summary(fit, standardised = TRUE) stops. update() still works on these fits, so fit <- update(fit) fits the model again when the data are found.

  • In get_inlavaan_internal(), the field Sigma_theta is now Omega. It is the covariance matrix of the Laplace approximation, on the internal scale of the parameters. The new name agrees with the Omega argument of loo() and with the notation of the documentation, where Sigma is the model-implied covariance matrix of the data. Code that reads Sigma_theta must now read Omega.

  • Deprecation warnings now have the class inlavaan_deprecated. The warning for the old Sigma argument of loo() has this class too, and still warns at every call. Arguments and values deprecated from this version on warn once per session, and options(inlavaan.deprecation = "error") makes them errors, so that tests can find old code. Their help has a “deprecated” badge.

  • When the check of the Hessian at the mode fails (the Jacobian of the gradient is not symmetric, or the Hessian on the fast path of the intercepts or from inlavaan_control(hessian = "forward") is not symmetric or differs from central differences of the gradient), the warning now says so in INLAvaan’s words, with the class inlavaan_hessian_warning. Before, it named the arguments of the engine (grad, logpost, hess), which INLAvaan users never give.

  • diagnostics() now gives the engine’s diagnostics, in the engine’s order, and then INLAvaan’s own: nsamp, psi_npd_share and theta_npd_share. Code that reads them by name still works, except for the changes below. Code that reads them by position may not. ?diagnostics explains each name.

    • scan_end_mass and scan_end_mass_max are now unscanned_mass and unscanned_mass_max. The old names are gone.
    • New global diagnostics: hess_cond_cor, grad_gap_max, vb_fallback, vb_step_max, vb_lhat, vb_j0, vb_j1, vb_solve, mean_gap_max, ridge_bend_max and n_heavy_tails. New per-parameter columns: grad_gap, vb_step_sigma, mean_gap, gamma1, tails and ridge_bend.
    • grad_num, grad_diff, vb_mcse_max, vb_mcse_mean and vb_mcse_sigma are always NA, and will be removed in 0.5.0. grad_gap now checks the analytic gradient against finite differences.
    • The intercepts of a saturated mean structure have no scan, so their alpha, nmad and unscanned_mass are NA, where before they were 0, 0 and 6.3e-05.

  • The warning at the end of a fit now takes its checks, its levels and its bullets from the engine, in INLAvaan’s words, and adds INLAvaan’s checks of the convergence of nlminb() and of the latent and residual covariance matrices. New bullets say when the analytic gradient does not match the log-posterior (grad_gap above 0.1), when the VB correction did not settle (vb_step_max above 0.1), when the one-step VB correction failed its check (vb_solve is 1), when a marginal has heavy tails, and when the mode may be far from the posterior mass. When nlminb() does not converge, the warning now says what to try: to raise mode_maxit or mode_maxeval in inlavaan_control() when it stopped at one of these limits, and other starting values otherwise. It gives the message of nlminb() once. The check of the condition number now reads hess_cond_cor, which does not depend on the units of the parameters. Values in posterior SDs carry the unit σ, or “SD” where the console cannot show σ. The warning ends with a pointer to ?diagnostics. When a marginal with heavy tails is a loading of a factor that a marker identifies, the warning adds a hint to try std.lv = TRUE, because a marker that loads weakly gives the other loadings of its factor such tails. So some fits that were silent now warn: for example, a one-factor model of x1, x2 and x3 fitted to the first 50 rows of HolzingerSwineford1939, whose one-step VB correction fails its check.

  • verbose has a new meaning, as in inlavanilla. verbose = FALSE, now the default, prints one line per stage of the fit, as the old default verbose = TRUE did. verbose = TRUE adds the details of each stage. To print nothing, use silent = TRUE. verbose = TRUE with silent = TRUE gives an error. inlavaan_control(debug = TRUE) no longer sets verbose = TRUE, and no longer prints a check of the gradient at the mode.

  • The vignettes, the articles and the examples use the arguments of 0.4.0. They give silent = TRUE where they gave verbose = FALSE, and no deprecated argument or value. The introduction now describes the VB correction, marginal_scan and inlavaan_control(), and no longer the optimisers and the marginal methods that ended. The sampling article no longer compares copula and Gaussian draws, since samp_copula has no effect. The help of timing() says what the segments optim, vb and marginals hold, and that norta is about 0.

  • Thomas Luu is now listed as a copyright holder, for the skew-normal quantile approximation in qsnorm_fast() (Apache License 2.0).

  • fit_skew_normal() is now the engine’s version:

    • temp defaults to 1, not NA. The temperature is no longer estimated. temp = NA now gives an error. Give a positive number.
    • It returns xi, omega, alpha, logC and nmad. It no longer returns k and rmse, and its help no longer lists k and rsq (it never returned rsq).
    • It no longer rescales y to a maximum of 0. Give it y - max(y).
    • threshold_log_drop must be a single finite negative number, and temp a single finite positive number. Otherwise it gives an error. Before, threshold_log_drop = -Inf kept every point.
    • It always keeps the five highest points, also when fewer points lie above threshold_log_drop.
    • It fits from two starts and keeps the better fit. The second start is the mirror image of the first, with the opposite skew. With one start, a fit could stall near alpha = 0 when the marginal was almost symmetric. On the Holzinger and Swineford three-factor model and the Political Democracy model, no reported value moves by more than 5e-6 posterior SDs.

  • The help of fit_skew_normal_samp() now lists only the fields that it returns: xi, omega and alpha.

  • New psnorm() and qsnorm() give the distribution function and the quantile function of the skew normal. They share the help page of dsnorm(). qsnorm() refines qsnorm_fast() by Newton’s method. For tail probabilities of 1e-6 or more, psnorm(qsnorm(p)) returns p to a relative error of about 1e-10. As pnorm() and qnorm() do, they recycle their arguments to the longest, give a zero-length result when an argument has length zero, and keep the names and dimensions of q or p.

  • qsnorm_fast() gave wrong values when one call mixed values of alpha or p. Where alpha was 0, 1 or -1, it gave 0 in place of the quantile. Where alpha was negative but not -1, a p of 0 or 1 in a call with other values of p gave an infinite value with the wrong sign. Fits were not affected: inlavaan() passes one alpha at a time and, in practice, never a p of exactly 0 or 1. qsnorm_fast() now recycles its arguments to the length of the longest, as qsnorm() does, and a zero-length argument gives a zero-length result. Before, an alpha longer than p gave NA or an error. The help of qsnorm_fast() no longer says that its relative error is below 1e-7. Against qsnorm(), its error is about 7e-3 times omega for p in [0.01, 0.99], and about 0.09 times omega for p in [1e-6, 1 - 1e-6]. Its help now also gives the error further out in the tails.

  • inlavaan() now checks the threshold of the skew-normal fit (inlavaan_control(log_threshold = ), or the deprecated sn_fit_logthresh) itself, for every marginal_method. Before, the check was inside fit_skew_normal(), and it ran only for marginal_method = "skewnorm". The threshold must be a finite negative number. Before, -Inf kept every scan point. It now gives an error. To keep every scan point, give a large negative number, such as -100.

  • summary() now uses the exact skew-normal quantile, qsnorm(), in place of the approximation qsnorm_fast(). The posterior draws now use a spline of the exact quantile (sn_score_map(), accurate to about 1e-6 posterior SDs) in place of qsnorm_fast(). With the default settings, on the Holzinger and Swineford three-factor model and the Political Democracy model, over 150 seeds:

    • For the rows that come from the fitted marginals, the Mean, SD and Mode do not change. Their quantiles move by at most 0.008 posterior SDs on the Holzinger and Swineford model, and by at most 0.006 posterior SDs on the Political Democracy model.
    • The rows that come from the draws (covariances and defined parameters) change for the same seed. With the old fit of fit_skew_normal_samp(), no Mean, SD, Mode or quantile of these rows moved by more than 0.01 posterior SDs in about 19 fits of 20. In the other fits, a row moved by up to about 0.15 posterior SDs, where the old fit stalled near alpha = 0 for one set of draws and not for the other. With the new fit (next item), a row moves by more than 0.01 posterior SDs in 1 of these 300 fits, by 0.011 posterior SDs. The next item also gives the change since INLAvaan 0.3.5, with both changes together.
    • DIC moves by about 0.06 (at most 0.084), and PPP by at most 0.006. The marginal likelihood (mloglik) and Dhat do not change.

  • fit_skew_normal_samp() now fits from up to three starts and keeps the fit with the largest likelihood. Two starts come from the skewness of the draws, as in fit_skew_normal(): the moment-based shape and its mirror image, with the opposite skew. When the sample skewness is below about 0.0018 in absolute value, these two starts are alpha of about 0.58 and -0.58. The third start is the old one, alpha = 0, where the likelihood has a stationary point. It runs only when the fits from the first two starts end on the same side of alpha = 0, or when one of them is not finite. When they end on opposite sides, the old fit is not computed, so the new fit is not guaranteed by construction to have a likelihood at least that of the old fit. On all the draws below, its likelihood is at least that of the old fit, up to rounding (a relative difference of at most 4e-15). The optimiser uses the analytic gradient and Hessian of the likelihood. For mildly skewed draws, the old fit could stall near alpha = 0, at alpha of about 0.01, and a small change in the draws could tip it to the optimum, at alpha of about 1. The covariances and defined parameters in summary() come from this fit, so they could jump. For draws that do not vary or are not all finite, the fit returns the same values as before, with one warning in place of the warnings of nlminb() (and now also for empty draws). With the default settings, on the Holzinger and Swineford three-factor model and the Political Democracy model (also with two defined parameters added), over 150 seeds each:

    • For the same draws, a row changes only where the old fit stalled (alpha within 0.05 of 0): 40 of 450 covariances of the Holzinger and Swineford model, 37 of 900 covariances of the Political Democracy model and 139 of 300 defined parameters. The new fit stalls for none of them. The other rows move by at most 3e-5 posterior SDs. Where the old fit stalled, the Mean and SD move by at most 0.0012 posterior SDs, the quantiles by up to 0.18 posterior SDs and the Mode by up to 0.2 posterior SDs. A row moves by more than 0.01 posterior SDs in 36 of 150 fits of the Holzinger and Swineford model, in 37 of 150 fits of the Political Democracy model, and in 109 of 150 fits with the defined parameters.
    • Together with the exact quantile in summary() and in the draws (item above), against INLAvaan 0.3.5, a row from the draws moves by more than 0.01 posterior SDs in about 1 fit of 4 of the Holzinger and Swineford and the Political Democracy models, and in about 3 fits of 4 with the defined parameters. Most of this change comes from the new fit.
    • On these models, the fit is now stable when the draws change a little. With the draws of qsnorm_fast() in place of those of qsnorm(), a row moved by more than 0.01 posterior SDs in 7, 1 and 7 fits of 150 (Holzinger and Swineford, Political Democracy, and with the defined parameters), by up to 0.12 posterior SDs. Now 1, 0 and 0 fits do. That one fit moves by 0.011 posterior SDs, and the old fit moves by the same amount there. With one draw of noise of 1e-3 posterior SDs added to the draws, 5, 2 and 10 fits of 150 moved by more than 0.01 posterior SDs, by up to 0.2 posterior SDs. These counts are approximate, because they change with the draw of the noise: other draws gave from 4 to 9, from 3 to 8 and from 9 to 21 fits, by up to 0.24 posterior SDs. Now no fit does, for each of six draws of the noise, and no row moves by more than 0.0005 posterior SDs.
    • For near-symmetric, heavy-tailed draws, such as draws from a t distribution with 8 degrees of freedom, two fits of opposite skew can have almost the same likelihood. The fit can then still switch between them when the draws change a little, and move a row by up to about 0.05 posterior SDs.
    • The draws, the rows from the fitted marginals, mloglik, DIC and PPP do not change, and neither does the random number stream.
    • On posterior draws of these models, the fit of one row of 1000 draws takes about 1.1 ms, in place of about 4 ms in INLAvaan 0.3.5 (and about 12 ms in the development version before the analytic derivatives).

  • approx_data in get_inlavaan_internal() no longer has the columns k and rmse. k was the temperature of the skew-normal fit, and rmse was a mean squared error, not its root. For skew-normal marginals, the columns are now xi, omega, alpha, logC, nmad and gamma1, and each row is built by name.

INLAvaan 0.3.5

New features

  • Priors on variances accept the [var] qualifier, for example prior("gamma(1,1)[var]"), which puts the prior on the variance. blavaan reads [var] the same way, so one syntax now gives the same prior in both packages.

  • A gamma prior with no qualifier on a variance gives a message, once per session. INLAvaan reads it as a prior on the variance, whereas blavaan reads it as a prior on the precision. The meaning in INLAvaan is unchanged.

  • Fits with missing data (missing = "ml") are faster, most of all under planned missingness: the log-likelihood and its gradient now factorise each missing-data pattern directly.

  • The new hessian_method = "forward" builds the Hessian at the posterior mode with about half the gradient evaluations, for large models.

Bug fixes

  • The VB correction of models with more than 300 free parameters, or with n_qmc above 128, changed from run to run, even with set.seed(). It is now the same on every run. These models need the spacefillr package, which INLAvaan now suggests in place of qrng.

  • With cov_as_cor = TRUE, loo() and waic() called after the fit scored the wrong model. The returned parameter table relabelled the covariances as correlations, so they were not scaled by their standard deviations. On the Holzinger and Swineford three-factor model, LOOIC was 7664 instead of 7538. The classes now stay covariances, and the setting is stored in get_inlavaan_internal(fit)$cov_as_cor.

  • Under std.ov = TRUE, residual covariances were treated as correlations although the residual variances are free. Under std.lv = TRUE, latent covariances were treated as correlations also when a latent variance was free (for example in a second group, c(1, NA)*f). The covariance was then held in (-1, 1), and the correlation prior acted on the covariance. These rows are now covariances, scaled by their standard deviations, with the prior on the correlation. Results change for such models. They now equal the fit of the same model written out without std.ov or std.lv.

  • A prior string that does not parse, such as gama(1,1) or normal(0), now stops with an error that names the parameter and the prior. Before, it gave NA hyperparameters and failed later with an error about the gradient.

  • The README compared INLAvaan and blavaan under different priors on the latent variances, because the two packages read an unqualified gamma prior on different scales. The README now uses [var].

  • Models with exploratory blocks (efa()) now stop with an error. INLAvaan has no rotation, so it used to fit them and report loadings that are not identified.

  • Results no longer depend on the collation locale. The canonical parameter order, which sets the whitening of the posterior marginals, followed LC_COLLATE. Under a UTF-8 locale, models whose parameter names sort differently than in the C locale (mixed case, or the operators ~ and ~~) gave slightly different results. The README model, for example, had a marginal log-likelihood of -1644.364 under UTF-8 and -1644.390 under C. All locales now give the C result.

Internal

  • The MCMC validation scripts in inst/validation-tests/ moved out of the package, which no longer ships them. Their fast checks are now package tests: results do not depend on the order of the latent variables, and four smoke tests (equal covariances across groups, std.lv with a free second-group variance, a latent change score model, a cyclic model).

INLAvaan 0.3.4

CRAN release: 2026-11-13

New features

  • The fit now checks that the latent and residual covariance matrices are positive definite, at the posterior estimates and in the posterior draws. Each correlation is kept in (-1, 1), but a block of several free correlations can still be indefinite. diagnostics() reports the share of draws that are not positive definite (psi_npd_share, theta_npd_share), and the fit-time warning flags estimates that are not positive definite and shares above 0.01.

Bug fixes

  • compare() now warns when the models score different variables, for instance when they differ in fixed.x, since their marginal likelihoods and DICs are then not comparable.

  • Models with a single free parameter now fit (#32).

INLAvaan 0.3.3

CRAN release: 2026-10-26

New features

  • INLAvaan now fits two-level models with random slopes, which lavaan specifies with the rv() modifier. They work with compare(), loo(), waic(), logLik(), predict(), simulate() and sampling(), and summary() marks the rows that carry a random slope. fitted(), residuals() and the standardised estimates use the implied moments averaged over the covariates, and per_cluster = TRUE gives those of each cluster. The Bayesian fit indices are scaled against an unrestricted random-coefficient model. The posterior predictive p-value is not available and is dropped from test. A random slope on a latent or split covariate uses lavaan’s quadrature, which is slower, and integration.ngh sets its number of nodes. Such fits have no simulate(), casewise values, predict(type = "yhat"), per_cluster = TRUE or Bayesian fit indices. Composites cannot be combined with random slopes yet. See the multilevel article.

  • INLAvaan now fits composites, which lavaan specifies with the <~ operator, with continuous data, in one or more groups or at either level of a two-level model. They work with the fit measures, loo(), compare(), predict() and sampling(), and summary() gives posterior summaries for the variance and intercept of each composite. Free weights have the new default prior wmat = "normal(0,10)" in priors_for(). Unlike lavaan, INLAvaan estimates the (co)variances of the indicators by default (composites.cov = "free"); composites.cov = "fixed" fixes them at their sample values. See the new article on composites.

  • Composite models that INLAvaan cannot fit yet stop with an error: ordinal data, and composites.cov = "fixed" in two-level models. So do composite specifications that cannot be estimated as written, such as a free latent mean that only composites measure (as in agrowth() on composites).

Bug fixes

  • The posterior predictive p-value of two-level models was often close to 0 for models that fit. It now follows blavaan’s two-level PPP: each posterior draw generates replicate data, which are scored against the saturated model. The new arguments ppp_method and ppp_nsamp set how the data are scored (by default one Fisher-scoring step towards the saturated fit) and how many draws are used (250). The two-level PPP is experimental.

  • simulate() on a two-level fit now keeps the clusters of the data, with their labels and sizes, and no longer warns on every data set.

  • BCFI was -Inf or NaN for posterior draws whose independence model fits within its degrees of freedom. Such draws now follow lavaan’s CFI convention.

  • standardisedsolution() ignored its nsamp argument and summarised as many posterior draws as the fit itself had used.

  • Multigroup models with missing = "ml" gave wrong posteriors.

  • loo() and waic() gave wrong values for complete-data two-level models in which the two levels list the variables in different orders, for example when a regression appears at one level only.

  • compare() failed when a model was given as a long call.

  • sampling(prior = TRUE) with type = "observed" or type = "all" rejected every draw in models with an observed outcome or covariate.

  • The marginal log-likelihood was too low by about half the number of free parameters when vb_correction = TRUE (the default). As a result, Bayes factors from compare() favoured models with fewer parameters.

  • A defined parameter (:=) can now use other defined parameters, in any order, as in lavaan. Previously the fit failed with an “object not found” error.

  • Defined parameters that are constant, or that cannot be computed for some posterior draws (such as log(b) when b can be negative), no longer stop the fit. Their summaries use the draws where they can be computed, and a single warning gives the share left out, in place of R’s repeated “NaNs produced” warnings.

  • summary() showed the wrong SD, credible interval and prior for defined parameters, and for some rows after them, when the model had equality constraints (shared labels or group.equal).

  • Equality constraints written as a == b or a == <number> are now honoured. Previously they were ignored, along with shared labels and group.equal in the same model. Constraints INLAvaan cannot fit (such as a == 2*b, a > 0, effect.coding, or a loading held equal to a variance) now give an error.

  • Covariances held equal (by shared labels or group.equal) now fit correctly. Previously their posterior was biased, or the fit failed.

  • sampling() and simulate() now work for models with equality constraints, and simulate() for multigroup models.

  • Parameter names now match coef(). Previously plot(fit, params = ) could not find multigroup := parameters, and labels such as lag1 were mangled. A := parameter that reuses a parameter label, and multigroup two-level models, now give an error.

  • Data with ordered-factor columns are now fitted as ordinal data, as with ordered =. Previously the fit failed. ordered = naming variables outside the model no longer widens the posterior, and a name that matches no model variable gives an error.

  • predict(newdata = ) for ordinal models now codes the categories as in the fit. Previously factor columns gave an error and 0/1 codes gave wrong factor scores.

  • Chained modifiers in the model syntax are now all kept. Previously only one survived, so prior("normal(0,1)")*a*x2 lost its prior, 0.5*a*x2 was left free and NA*a*x1 stayed fixed.

  • A prior() on any of several parameters held equal is now used. Previously only a prior on the first of them counted.

  • Models where only one variance enters a covariance (for example, with the other variance fixed) no longer fail.

  • predict() now works for models with observed covariates or observed outcomes, including with conditional.x = TRUE. Factor scores and fitted values for models with latent regressions now match lavaan.

  • Two-level models with named levels (level: within / level: between) now fit, and their parameter names follow coef().

  • vcov() now matches coef() in length, order and names for models with equality constraints, and lavInspect(fit, "vcov") works on such fits.

  • predict() no longer fails when a variance is zero, for example a residual variance fixed to zero, or a latent variable fully determined by such an indicator.

  • loo() and waic() no longer fail on two-level models fitted with missing = "ML" that have between-level variables, such as cluster-level covariates.

  • loo() and waic() now score two-level fixed.x = TRUE models correctly when they mix covariates at both levels with within-only ones.

  • fit_skew_normal_samp(), and with it the summaries of covariances and defined parameters (:=), missed the skew of draws with a small SD (below about 0.2). Posterior modes are also more accurate for parameters on a small scale.

  • loo() and waic() on FIML fits with fixed.x covariates now score the outcomes given the covariates, as for complete data. Previously two-level FIML scores included the covariates’ density, so they could not be compared with listwise fits or across covariate sets.

  • loo() and waic() no longer fail on FIML fits with singleton or two-row clusters, or with clusters or rows that have no observed data. Units with nothing to predict are left out, with a message. In two-level type = "loso", rows with no within-level data no longer each count the whole cluster.

  • predict(type = "ypred") for two-level models now adds residual noise to observed outcomes, not only to factor indicators.

  • predict() for two-level models now draws latent variables and missing values from their posterior given all of the cluster’s data, as for single-level models. Previously it returned factor scores without their uncertainty, and imputed each row without the rest of its cluster.

  • With fixed.x = TRUE (the default), the marginal likelihood and DIC now condition on the covariates. Previously a covariate with no effect changed Bayes factors from compare(), by a lot in two-level models where it varies at both levels.

  • fitMeasures() overstated the chi-square of models without a mean structure, and with it BRMSEA and the other Bayesian fit indices.

  • The PPP no longer fails for conditional.x = TRUE fits.

  • The PPP no longer overstates the fit of models with fixed covariates (fixed.x = TRUE, the default). Its replicates varied the covariates, which the model does not predict.

  • simulate() and predict(type = "ymis") now work for conditional.x = TRUE fits. Previously simulate() rejected every draw and imputation failed.

  • sampling() for conditional.x = TRUE fits now draws the covariates too, as for other fits. Previously it left out their effects.

  • Models with a free covariance above 1 at its starting value, such as covariances between covariates under fixed.x = FALSE, no longer fail.

Minor improvements and fixes

  • Models without a mean structure fit much faster. The gradient of their marginalised log-likelihood is now lavaan’s ML gradient for n - 1 observations and the unbiased sample covariance, where INLAvaan used to rebuild lavaan’s Jacobian of the implied covariance at every call. The posterior is unchanged, and a 256-parameter factor model fits about ten times faster. Such a model with sampling weights now gives an error when a group’s weights sum to 1 or less, where the marginalised likelihood is unbounded.

  • likelihood = "wishart", also the default under mimic = "EQS" or "LISREL", is now ignored with a message. lavaan then divides the sample covariance by n - 1, but INLAvaan’s likelihood assumes the divisor n, so such fits overstated the sample covariance by n / (n - 1). Without a mean structure, integrating out the saturated means already gives the Wishart likelihood.

  • Parameter types missing from dp take their default priors, and a dp without names gives an error.

  • A Hessian that is not positive definite at the posterior mode gives a clear error.

  • plot() explains that fixed and derived parameters have no posterior density.

  • compare() warns when fits differ in vb_correction.

  • predict(newdata = ) warns about ordinal values not seen when fitting.

  • fitted(), residuals(), the standardised estimates and the R-square of random-slope fits also work with lavaan versions after 0.7-3.

INLAvaan 0.3.2

CRAN release: 2026-10-01

Deprecations

  • The Sigma argument of loo() is now Omega. The new name agrees with the notation for the posterior covariance in the documentation. You can still use Sigma, but you get a deprecation warning. If you supply the two names, you get an error.

Bug fixes

  • Single-level fits with missing = "ml" gave incorrect posterior summaries with the default skew-normal marginals. The loadings and variances were far from the FIML estimates, and the scan-endpoint check flagged almost all parameters. The cause was a shortcut that treats the free intercepts as separate from the covariance parameters. This is correct for complete data, but not under FIML. INLAvaan no longer uses the shortcut under FIML. These results were already correct:

    • The posterior mode and the Laplace covariance.
    • Fits with marginal_method = "marggaus", or with marginal_correction = "hessian" or "none".
    • Two-level FIML fits.

  • The posterior predictive p-value (PPP) was incorrect for data with missing values. For example, a correct model with 20% missing cells got a PPP of 0.000. The cause was that the PPP used a sample covariance that is not correct when values are missing. The PPP now uses the saturated (h1) covariance from lavaan:

    • For single-level FIML fits, this is the EM covariance.
    • For two-level fits, these are the within-level and between-level h1 covariances, with or without missing values.

    Single-level fits with complete data do not change. Two-level fits with complete data get slightly different PPP values.

  • The Bayesian fit indices had two errors:

    • For two-level models, the saturated log-likelihood was much too low. The deviance chi-square became negative, and INLAvaan set it to zero. As a result, BRMSEA was 0, BGammaHat was 1 and BTLI was more than 1. Two-level fits with missing = "ml" gave NA.
    • The count of sample moments included the moments of fixed exogenous covariates, but lavaan does not count these. As a result, BRMSEA and adjBGammaHat used slightly incorrect degrees of freedom for models with an observed predictor and fixed.x = TRUE.

    INLAvaan now gets the two values from lavaan. Single-level fits without covariates do not change.

  • The incremental fit indices BCFI, BTLI and BNFI used an incorrect baseline. compare() used its first model as the baseline, without a warning. Thus the first model got a score against itself, which is always zero, and the other models got a score against the first model, not against a null model. fitMeasures(), bfit_indices() and compare() now fit the independence model automatically, as lavaan does. In this model, each observed variable has its variance and intercept, and no variables correlate. The fit uses the same data and options as the model, and takes less than one second, also for 64 items. compare() fits it one time for all models. Other changes:

    • Use baseline.model to supply a different baseline, or baseline.model = FALSE to skip the incremental indices.
    • If baseline.model has the same free parameters as the model, you get a warning.
    • BTLI is now NA, not -Inf, when the ratio of the baseline is 1.

    The absolute indices (BRMSEA, BGammaHat, adjBGammaHat, BMc) do not change.

  • For two-level models, sampling() gave only the within-level part. All three types now draw from the full two-level model:

    • type = "latent" now includes the between-level latent variables.
    • type = "observed" now includes the between-level part and the between-only variables.
    • type = "implied" now gives the within-level and between-level covariances, not one covariance.

  • With marginal_method = "marggaus", the Mean and SD were incorrect for parameters on a transformed scale, such as variances and correlations. The Mean was the posterior median, and the SD came from the delta method. INLAvaan now calculates the two values as the moments of the transformed Gaussian marginal, with Gauss-Hermite quadrature. The quantiles, modes and densities do not change.

  • predict() did not draw its parameter sample in the same way as the rest of the package. It did not use the NORTA correlation adjustment, and it ignored the samp_copula setting of the fit. Thus the factor scores and predicted values had a different dependence structure from the posterior draws of the fit. predict() now uses the stored correlation matrix and the samp_copula setting of the fit.

  • timing() gave a total that was too large. It added the lavaan setup time two times, because this time is already part of init. The segments now do not overlap, and their sum agrees with system.time(). timing() no longer shows the start_time stamp as a duration. The documentation now includes the loo and waic segments.

  • loo() removed the units without a second-order term from elpd_loo, p_loo and their standard errors. Thus the sum had fewer units, and the model looked better than it is. loo() now keeps all the units:

    • If the log CPO term of a unit does not exist at second order (k_max >= 1), loo() gives all estimates at first order, for all units. Thus each estimate uses one order only. loo() and fitmeasures() give a warning that names these units.
    • If the lpd term of a unit does not exist at second order, the unit adds its first-order difference to p_loo. elpd_loo and looic do not change. This case is usual in SEM fits and the error is small, thus there is no warning. The printed result shows a note, and n_lpd_ok gives the count.

    This changes elpd_loo and looic for fits with a unit at k_max >= 1. Without such a unit, the other data and the prior cannot identify some combination of the parameters. Thus, examine such units.

  • compare() calculated se_diff from per-unit values that did not agree with elpd_diff. The paired variance did not include the units without a second-order term, but the ELPD totals included them. The two values now use the same per-unit values.

  • compare(loo = TRUE) now uses the same Taylor order for all models. This is the highest order that all the models can supply. Before, it could compare a model at second order with a model at first order. Thus part of elpd_diff came from the change of order, not from the models. The table shows the order.

  • test = "loo" stored the LOO but not the WAIC, but the documentation said that it stores the two. A request for the LOO or the WAIC now stores the two (see the test entry under New features).

New features

  • New vb_method argument to inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth() sets the integration rule for the VB mean correction:

    • "sobol" (the default) uses the scrambled Sobol rule with n_qmc nodes, as before.
    • "gauss_hermite" uses a deterministic three-point Gauss-Hermite rule along each principal axis of the Laplace covariance. This is 2m + 1 nodes for m free parameters.

    The Gauss-Hermite rule gives the same shift on each run. On the benchmark models, it was more accurate than the default 64-node rule. It is faster than the default for fewer than approximately 30 free parameters, and slower for more. It gives no quadrature error, thus vb_mcse_sigma is NA. This feature is experimental.

  • diagnostics() has new values:

    • Global: vb_shift_max, the largest VB mean correction in posterior-SD units, and scan_end_mass_max, the largest scan_end_mass.
    • For each parameter: scan_end_mass (see the next entry), and alpha, the shape of the fitted skew-normal.

  • New diagnostic scan_end_mass. It is the probability that the fitted skew-normal marginal puts outside the scan window, which is four posterior SDs on each side of the mode. INLAvaan fits the marginal only inside this window, thus the mass outside it is an extrapolation. A large value shows that the credible limits of the parameter are not reliable.

    • A Gaussian marginal gives 6.3e-05. Good fits give values from 1e-03 to 1e-02.
    • The fit gives a warning if a parameter has a value more than 0.05. The warning names a maximum of three parameters.
    • The value is NA unless marginal_method = "skewnorm".
    • The calculation is closed-form, thus it adds no cost.

  • New samp_norta argument to inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth() enables or disables the NORTA correlation adjustment of the skew-normal copula. It is independent of samp_copula. The default is FALSE, because the adjustment does not change the marginals and has a very small effect: on the benchmark models, it changed no correlation by more than 0.01. predict() uses the same setting as the fit.

  • The test argument of inlavaan(), acfa(), asem() and agrowth() now gives the set of post-estimation values to calculate:

    • The basic values are "ppp", "dic", "loo" and "waic".
    • "standard" (or "default") is c("ppp", "dic"). "full" is all four. "none" is nothing.
    • You can combine values, for example test = c("standard", "loo").
    • An unknown value gives an error. This includes the test names of lavaan, for example "satorra.bentler". Before, lavaan ignored these values without a warning.

    You can now request the PPP and the DIC separately. For example, test = "dic" gives the DIC without the PPP.

    The default no longer calculates the LOO and the WAIC. Before, the default calculated the LOO if its predicted time was less than 10 seconds. Thus the fit time was difficult to predict. INLAvaan now calculates the LOO and the WAIC only on request ("loo", "waic" or "full"). If the model does not support them (PML or ordinal data, conditional.x = TRUE, multigroup two-level models), you get a warning and the fit continues without them.

    To get elpd_loo in fitmeasures(fit) as before, use test = "full" or add_loo(fit). add_loo() now stores the LOO and the WAIC (before, it stored only the LOO). loo(fit) and waic(fit) still calculate on request.

  • cores > 1 now works in all front ends. Before, the parallel stages of inlavaan() and loo() used mclapply() to fork worker processes. Forks are not available on Windows. They are also not safe in threaded IDE sessions, such as RStudio and Positron, where the child processes can stop without a message. INLAvaan now uses a PSOCK cluster (separate R processes) when forks are not safe.

  • New cov_as_cor argument to inlavaan(). INLAvaan always estimates the residual and latent covariances (theta_cov, psi_cov) on the correlation scale. By default, it then reports them on the covariance scale from a posterior sample, as lavaan and blavaan do. With cov_as_cor = TRUE, INLAvaan reports the correlation-scale marginals directly, as theta_cor and psi_cor. Use this option to compare the marginals with a reference on the correlation scale. The estimation does not change.

  • waic() is now deterministic. It calculates the two WAIC terms in closed form from the Laplace summary, with the same per-unit Taylor values as loo(). It no longer uses posterior draws. This changes the estimand, thus p_waic and waic change for all existing fits. The change is largest at small N. Other changes:

    • The results are exactly reproducible, and do not depend on a seed.
    • The nsamp argument is removed. If you supply it, you get a warning.
    • The new second_order argument works as in loo(). At first order, the WAIC and the LOO are identical.
    • The p_waic > 0.4 rule is removed. It was an empirical threshold for the variation of the old estimator, with no theory to support it.
    • The second-order WAIC exists only if the lpd term exists for all units (k_min > -1). If not, waic() gives all estimates at first order, with a warning.
    • At fit time, the WAIC comes from the same calculation as the LOO, at no extra cost.
    • The per_unit table of loo() has two new columns: k_ssq, which is part of the WAIC penalty, and k_min, the existence check for the lpd term.

  • loo() now gives two curvature diagnostics for each unit, k_max and k_sum. It calculates them in closed form from the Laplace summary, not from posterior draws. k_max is the fraction of the posterior precision that the unit has along its worst direction. The second-order term of the unit exists only if k_max < 1. k_sum is the total leverage of the unit. loo() applies no threshold to these values.

Minor improvements and fixes

  • loo() no longer uses the name “effective number of parameters” for two different values:

    • p_loo has the same definition as in the loo package. It stays in the estimates table.
    • The sum of the per-unit k_sum is now pd_trace, the trace form of the DIC pD.

    The printed result also shows a new curvature check. It compares the total gap between the first-order and second-order estimates (elpd_gap) with half of pD. A large excess shows that the second-order expansion is not stable. The documentation now also tells you to use second_order = FALSE only for diagnostics or to decrease cost. A first-order score is too high by approximately half of pD, thus it cannot compare models of different sizes.

  • loo() and waic() results now print under a cli rule that shows the number of units, the number of groups and the Taylor order. This rule replaces the “Computed from …” line. The notes now fit the width of the console. summary() on these results is the same as print().

  • INLAvaan now requires lavaan >= 0.7-2. Thus the compatibility layer for older lavaan versions is removed. The warning about the two-level FIML gradient for cases with all within-level values missing is also removed, because lavaan >= 0.7-1.2707 corrects this problem.

  • The default "nlminb" optimiser now uses iter.max = 1000 and eval.max = 2000. The nlminb() defaults (150 and 200) were too small for some complex models. When the optimiser reached these limits, only diagnostics() or a fit-time warning showed it. Values that you supply in control still have priority.

INLAvaan 0.3.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-21

Bug fixes

  • The timing() function did not return the correct total time due to a breaking name change in lavaan.
  • Fixed CRAN errors and notes on certain linux builds relating to .Rd usage and
    convergence checks.

INLAvaan 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-07-11

New features

  • loo() computes leave-one-out cross-validation from a single fit without refitting nor sampling, via a Taylor approximation of the case-deletion posterior: per-subject (LOSO) for single-level models, per-cluster (LOCO) for two-level models. Reports first- and second-order estimates and pointwise contributions, with opt-in parallelism (cores) and theta/Sigma overrides for scoring conditioned posterior summaries in user-built model-search workflows.
  • waic() computes the widely applicable information criterion from posterior draws, with pointwise contributions and reliability warnings.
  • Both criteria score fits with exogenous covariates on the likelihood they were fitted with: jointly with the covariates (fixed.x = FALSE) or conditionally on them (fixed.x = TRUE, the lavaan default; exact, no additional approximation), for any covariate placement, including cluster-level and within-level covariates in two-level models. The two flavours are never comparable, as conditional comparisons may differ in their covariate sets, which enables covariate selection.
  • loo() and waic() support multigroup models. Groups are independent, so each unit is scored against its own group’s implied moments, under either mean treatment and either covariate flavour, with cross-group equality constraints (group.equal) flowing through automatically. Units are identified by case number and carry a group column, so results keep their identity across fits that stack groups differently. Multigroup two-level models are not supported yet.
  • loo() and waic() support fits estimated by full-information maximum likelihood (missing = "ml"). Single-level units are scored on the entries they actually have – the observed-data predictive log p(y_i,obs | D_-i) – with casewise kernels evaluated per missing pattern, so a unit with fewer observed entries self-weights in the elpd. Two-level fits are scored per cluster (LOCO), each cluster on its observed-data marginal likelihood via lavaan’s raw-data cluster kernels (no per-cluster sufficient statistics, since LOCO deletes whole clusters). This shares the missing-at-random assumption of the FIML fit itself. Multigroup two-level models remain unsupported under missingness.
  • On two-level models loo() and waic() gain type = "loso", scoring the conditional predictive (leave-one-unit-out: a new observation within an observed cluster) instead of the default marginal predictive (type = "loco", leave-one-cluster-out: a new cluster). These are the two estimands of Merkle, Furr & Rabe-Hesketh (2019); they answer different questions and are easily conflated, so the marginal is the default and the conditional warns. loo() uses the Taylor expansion and waic() the posterior draws, computing the same estimand two ways; both work with and without missing data. (waic() previously had no type.)
  • fitmeasures() gains elpd_loo, se_loo, p_loo, looic and elpd_waic, se_waic, p_waic, waic: included in "all" when stored with the fit, computed on demand when requested by name.
  • compare() gains loo = TRUE. Models sorted by descending ELPD, with p_loo and ELPD differences with paired standard errors (mixed-flavour comparisons are refused). Pairing matches units by id rather than row order, so a pooled fit can be compared against a multigroup fit of the same data, and the measurement-invariance ladder (configural, metric, scalar) is compared on a proper predictive scale.
  • Both criteria can be computed at fit time and stored with the fit. The default test = "standard" does so automatically for supported models with a mean structure. The WAIC reuses the fit’s own posterior draws (when nsamp >= 100), and the LOO runs when its predicted serial cost is within a 10-second budget. test = "loo" forces the LOO regardless of the budget, test = "none" skips everything, and fit <- add_loo(fit) stores it post hoc. Stored results are reused by loo(), waic(), fitmeasures(), and compare().
  • fitted() (and fitted.values()) return the model-implied moments of an INLAvaan fit, evaluated at the posterior means, matching the lavaan and blavaan output structure. type = "ov" gives casewise predicted values.
  • predict() gains a summary argument; summary = TRUE collapses the posterior draws and returns point estimates directly, equivalent to summary(predict(...)) in one call. Default FALSE, so existing code is unaffected.
  • residuals() (and resid()) return the observed-minus-fitted moments of an INLAvaan fit, matching the lavaan and blavaan output structure and supporting all lavaan residual types (raw, cor, cor.bentler, normalized, standardized) plus type = "casewise".
  • anova() on an INLAvaan fit now errors, pointing to compare(). Unlike fitted()/residuals()/predict(), this is a deliberate departure from blavaan (which silently inherits lavaan’s frequentist likelihood-ratio test): there is no direct Bayesian analogue of that test, and compare() already provides the appropriate tools (Bayes factors, DIC/pD, LOO/WAIC).
  • logLik() returns the Laplace-approximated marginal log-likelihood (log evidence) by default, printed with a note that it is not comparable to a classical log-likelihood; type = "plugin" instead returns the classical log-likelihood at the posterior mean, with df/nobs attributes so it supports AIC()/BIC() at the point estimate.
  • deviance() is new for INLAvaan fits (lavaan has no deviance() at all). Follows the BUGS/JAGS/Stan convention: type = "mean" (default) returns the posterior mean deviance with pD/DIC attached as attributes; type = "plugin" returns the deviance at the posterior mean (matching -2 * logLik(type = "plugin")). Both require test != "none".
  • AIC()/BIC() on an INLAvaan fit now error, documented alongside logLik(). Both are large-sample asymptotic approximations to quantities INLAvaan already computes directly – AIC approximates predictive accuracy (loo()/waic()), BIC approximates -2 * log(marginal likelihood) (logLik()) – so reporting them at the posterior mean would be a cruder proxy for numbers already available. The point estimate remains available for reporting-convention purposes via AIC(logLik(object, type = "plugin")) / BIC(...).
  • Fits now self-check their diagnostics: inlavaan() warns once, at the end of the fit, if the optimiser did not converge, the gradient at the reported mode is materially non-zero (Newton step > 0.1 posterior SD), a skew-normal marginal fits poorly (NMAD > 0.1), the VB correction shifted a posterior mean by more than 1 posterior SD, or the Hessian is near-singular – naming the offending parameters. A healthy fit stays silent; suppress via the inlavaan_diagnostics_warning condition class. diagnostics() gains the scale-free mode_shift_max (global) and mode_shift_sigma (per-parameter) measures backing the gradient check. (#18)

Minor improvements and fixes

  • Saturated-means fast path: when the mean structure is saturated (all intercepts free and unconstrained with normal priors, no nonzero latent means), the posterior is exactly block-diagonal between the intercepts and the covariance parameters at the mode. The Hessian intercept block is now computed analytically with an exact zero cross block (finite differences run over the covariance columns only), and the skew-normal marginal scans skip the intercept axes, emitting their exact Gaussian marginals directly. About 25% faster on typical CFA/SEM fits, with results identical to within finite-difference noise.
  • Improved messaging for inlavaan() fit calls.

Bug fixes

  • standardisedsolution() and summary(standardized = TRUE) no longer silently drop their arguments under lavaan >= 0.7-1, which renamed several exported arguments (e.g. cov.std to cov_std, GLIST to glist). INLAvaan now resolves the spelling the installed lavaan expects once per session at load, working across lavaan versions.
  • Two-level FIML loo()/waic() scores are now correct for clusters containing a case fully missing on the within-level variables. lavaan retains such cases but its analytic gradient kernel mishandles the zero-observed pattern; INLAvaan drops these rows before the cluster kernels (exact for the marginal likelihood). Two-level FIML fitting also inherits the upstream gradient issue (fixed in lavaan PR #581), so inlavaan() warns when such cases are present on lavaan versions before the fix.
  • Models fitted with meanstructure = FALSE now use a proper Bayesian likelihood. See “Mean structures” vignette for details, including when model comparisons across the two mean treatments are meaningful.
    • The saturated means are given flat priors and marginalised analytically (closed form), replacing lavaan’s profiled likelihood, which is not a valid Bayesian object.
    • Posterior modes recalibrate by the factor n/(n-1) on the covariance side.
    • loo() and waic() score such fits on the exact exchangeable case-deletion conditionals. The previous zero-mean fallback and its warning are gone, and absolute ELPD values are meaningful and comparable with meanstructure = TRUE fits.
    • Posterior predictive draws include the saturated means and their mean-uncertainty.
    • Requesting meanstructure = FALSE for a two-level model now warns and fits with meanstructure = TRUE (the mean structure is required there).
    • The conditional (fixed.x = TRUE) flavour — the default for SEM with exogenous covariates — is fully supported: the mean marginalisation factorises blockwise, so each unit is scored by the difference of two exchangeable conditionals, with the frozen-covariate term entering as an exact constant.
  • predict() now centres the conditioning data on the model-implied means (or the saturated sample means when the model has no mean structure) when drawing factor scores and predicted observed variables. Previously the kernels conditioned on raw data, offsetting every factor score by a constant that grows with the variable means.
  • sampling() and simulate() draws of observed variables from models without a mean structure now include the saturated (sample) means, so posterior predictive replicates live on the data scale instead of being centred at zero.
  • sampling() and simulate() no longer error for models with a single latent variable, and their saturated-mean recovery is now robust to missing data (replicate columns were previously NA under missing = "pairwise").
  • The PPP’s observed discrepancy now uses the unbiased (divisor n-1) sample covariance, matching the scale of the Wishart-replicated covariances it is compared against; previously the divisor-n form made the PPP very slightly optimistic (an O(1/n) effect, all models).
  • coef() (and the merged parameter table, fitted values, and implied moments) now reports covariance parameters on the covariance scale. Previously these slots carried the posterior-mean correlation, while summary() showed the correct sample-based covariance; the discrepancy is visible whenever the relevant standard deviations are far from 1.

INLAvaan 0.2.5

CRAN release: 2026-06-11

Minor improvements and fixes

  • INLAvaan now works with both the current lavaan 0.6 series and the upcoming lavaan 0.7, which renames many of its internal functions. The lavaan internals INLAvaan relies on are now resolved when the package loads, under whichever naming scheme is available. lavaan (>= 0.6-19) is now declared explicitly, and the package is checked against the oldest supported, current CRAN, and development versions of lavaan on CI.
  • Fixed the trapezoid rule used by compare_mcmc() for density normalisation, overlap, and KL divergence computations.
  • compare_mcmc() and diagnostics() are now robust to NA values in density and diagnostic computations.
  • The dp argument of inlavaan() and friends is now documented in terms of priors_for().

INLAvaan 0.2.4

CRAN release: 2026-04-03

New features

  • bfit_indices() computes per-sample Bayesian fit index vectors (BRMSEA, BCFI, BTLI, BNFI), with summary() and print() methods. Summary statistics are also available via fitmeasures().
  • compare() compares two or more fitted models side by side, reporting marginal log-likelihood, Bayes factors, and DIC, with optional fit measures from fitmeasures().
  • diagnostics() computes global and per-parameter convergence and approximation-quality diagnostics for fitted models.
  • get_inlavaan_internal() is now exported and documented, providing access to the internal list stored in a fitted INLAvaan object.
  • predict() generates predictions for observed data and missing data imputation, respecting multilevel structure if present.
  • sampling() draws from the posterior (or prior) SEM generative model, returning parameter vectors, latent variables, or observed variables.
  • simulate() generates complete replicate datasets from a fitted model, useful for simulation-based calibration and posterior predictive checks.
  • timing() extracts wall-clock timings for individual computation stages of a fitted model.

Minor improvements and fixes

  • Cholesky factorisation of the precision matrix replaces raw solve() for covariance and log-determinant calculations.
  • Copula sampling with NORTA (NORmal To Anything) correlation adjustment is now the default (samp_copula = TRUE), ensuring posterior samples have correct skew-normal marginals and correct Pearson correlations.
  • Pre-computed Owen-scrambled Sobol sequences are used by default, with fallback to {qrng} for larger sequences. QMC sample size now scales with model dimension.
  • Skew-normal fitting now runs in parallel automatically when the number of marginals exceeds 120, using all available cores.
  • Small optimisations to the skew-normal volume correction.
  • acfa(), asem(), and agrowth() gain a vb_correction argument.
  • ggplot2 is now optional; plots fall back to base R graphics when it is not installed.
  • inlavaan() gains an sn_fit_ngrid argument to control the number of grid points per dimension when fitting skew-normal marginals (default 21).
  • inlavaan() now supports sn_fit_sample = TRUE for defined parameters, fitting a skew-normal approximation to their posterior marginals based on drawn samples.
  • plot() method gains improved visualisation options.
  • priors_for() now supports the [prec] scale qualifier for variance parameters (theta, psi), placing the prior on the precision scale with automatic Jacobian adjustment.
  • sampling() and simulate() gain a silent argument to suppress informational messages.
  • summary() now includes 25th and 75th percentile columns.
  • vcov() now returns the covariance matrix of the lavaan-side parameters and supports a type argument for choosing between sample and Laplace covariance.

Bug fixes

  • marginal_correction = "shortcut" no longer produces incorrect volume corrections.
  • qsnorm_fast() no longer incorrectly handles sign symmetries.

INLAvaan 0.2.3

CRAN release: 2026-01-28

  • Improved axis scanning, skewness correction, and VB mean correction routine.
  • Bug fixes for CRAN.
  • Updated README example.

INLAvaan 0.2.2

CRAN release: 2026-01-27

  • Under the hood, use lavaan’s MVN log-likelihood function to compute single- and multi-level log-likelihoods.
  • Added support for multi-level SEM models.
  • Added support for binary data using PML estimator from lavaan. NOTE: Ordinal is possible in theory, but the package still lacks proper prior support for the thresholds.
  • Added support for missing = "ML" to handle FIML for missing data.

INLAvaan 0.2.1

  • Support for lavaan 0.6-21.
  • Implemented variational Bayes mean correction for posterior marginals.
  • Defined parameters are now available, e.g. mediation analysis.
  • Prepare for CRAN release.

INLAvaan 0.2

  • INLAvaan has been rewritten from the ground up specifically for SEM models. The new version does not call R-INLA directly, but instead uses the core approximation ideas to fit SEM models more efficiently.
  • Features are restricted to normal likelihoods only and continuous observations for now.
  • Support for most models that lavaan/blavaan can fit, including CFA, SEM, and growth curve models.
  • Support for multigroup analysis.
  • Added PPP and DIC model fit indices.
  • Added prior specification for all model parameters.
  • Added support for fixed values and parameter constraints.
  • Initial CRAN submission.

INLAvaan 0.1

  • Used rgeneric functionality of R-INLA to implement a basic SEM framework.
